label: Bible Study
prompt: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be _____ again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
verse: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
note: Said to Nicodemus, who came by night — and promptly asked how a grown man manages it.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be _____.
verse: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
note: A promise for the 3 a.m. worrier: lie down unafraid, and the sleep itself shall be sweet.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the _____ of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:
verse: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:
note: Jesus' cure for worry: look at the lilies, which neither toil nor spin and still outdress Solomon.

label: Deep Water
prompt: For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a _____, and I know that I shall not be ashamed.
verse: For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed.
note: The Servant's resolve — echoed when Luke says Jesus 'stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem.'

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: For I _____ that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.
verse: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.
note: Paul runs the numbers — 'I reckon' — and present sufferings don't even compare to the glory ahead.
